svg.title: Copper Scroll entry 36: Valley of Shaveh
svg.text: Schematic plan, north up, with a cross-profile. One arrangement the text allows; not a reconstruction of any real site.
Project reading: a north-facing chamber in the south of the Shaveh’s fallow ground
Valley axis taken as north–south (not in the text), so ground “facing west” is its east slope.
Fallow upper slope over a lower irrigated floor: Puech 2015 pp. 73–74; Høgenhaven p. 75 n. 52.
Puech: the floor is “the low irrigated part” (entry 37)
not to scale; depth only labelled
Milik 1962: ha-Šoʾ = Bethso, a south-west necropolis
A north-facing hypogeum on the uncultivated west slope of
a ravine, in the Baqʿah necropolis (DJD p. 274).
Ravine and plain, SW of the city.
The slope is on the ravine’s west
is not recorded. The notes find it
שלף possibly a toponym (p. 265): no “fallow ground”, so
the fallow and irrigated pair with entry 37 falls away.
A named place in the Shaveh. “Facing
west, on the south” and the north-
or slope is meant is not given.
Drawn: chamber south of the place.
Readings that leave the plan as it is
Sum: the 65 shown matches no edition; Puech and Milik read 66,
Which valley: Puech, the King’s Valley towards Beth ha-Kerem;
צריח “chamber” is read by all the main editions; Allegro read
“In the fallow ground of the Shaveh, facing west, on the south, in the chamber facing north, dig
The Shaveh is a valley running north–south, so the fallow ground facing west is its east slope, and
“on the south” is the south part of that ground. The chamber opens to the north. Twenty-four cubits
are a digging depth in the chamber; no size or distance is given.
Atlas: best-supported, low. Candidates: Valley of Shaveh / King’s Valley (which valley is
unresolved), preferred, low; el-Baqʿa plain SW of the Old City, possible, low; Kidron valley at the
phase5_assessments.csv: Second Temple rock-cut tombs are reported in the Kidron (Avni & Greenhut
1996), with a “valley of the king” name (SWP III pp. 53–54); for el-Baqʿa only Milik’s statement.
Underground chambers fit either valley, and “fallow land” cannot be tested.
